newsitem.title: PARAGUAY: Farm workers on strike in Paraguay.
newsitem.headline: Farm workers on strike in Paraguay.

text.p: Some 20,000 Paraguayan farm workers converged on the capital Asuncion on Tuesday at the start of a two-day strike against free market policies they say have left them impoverished.

The workers have staged protests every March since 1994 against the administration of President Juan Carlos Wasmosy, which they say has not kept its promise to share land equitably and improve social services.
Paraguay has one of the lowest population densities in the region but 40 million acres (16 million hectares) of land belong to only 351 people, strike organisers said in a statement.

"Currently Paraguay has 980,000 underemployed people who the neo-liberals call 'micro-businessmen,' 500,000 people who for all practical purposes are illiterate, 40 percent of the population which is completely illiterate and over 1 million people who have no health care," the statement said.
Workers will spend the night in squares and parks surrounding Congress and march on Wednesday on the government palace. The government said it would post 9,000 troops outside the palace.

The workers on Tuesday denounced the murder of several of their leaders, an alleged alliance between "judges and government officials who are landowners," impunity, widespread corruption and scant state health and education services.

They are also demanding the release of some 100 activists who have been jailed in recent years and want the government to review economic policy, currently based on monetary stability and low inflation.

Twenty-one farm workers leaders have been killed since 1994 in clashes with security forces. After last year's protest, Wasmosy agreed to grant humanitarian aid to farm squatter settlements, legalise a variety of jobs, back production of food for family consumption and finance land purchases. He also agreed to draw up a medium and long-term development strategy.

The government began trumpeting its achievements just a few days ago and submitted a bill to Congress on related administrative issues. On Tuesday, the squares surrounding Congress where the workers are meeting were flanked by huge banners promoting government works.

The government says it has built 20 regional hospitals, handed out 30,000 land ownership titles, solved 91 land conflicts and granted financial aide to 250,000 small producers since Wasmosy took office in August 1993.
Surveys carried out by private groups in 1994 showed 84 percent of the rural population lived in extreme poverty.
